title: Iowans recognized at Governor's Lifesaving Awards for heroic actions - NewsBreak
text:
By Teodora Mitov ,
1 hours ago
DES MOINES, Iowa (WHO) — Four Iowans were honored at the Statehouse on Wednesday for saving lives during the annual Governor’s Lifesaving Awards.
The annual event is hosted by Governor Kim Reynolds and the Iowa Department of Public Safety.
It started in 1977 as a way to recognize Iowans who performed heroic acts in an attempt to save someone’s life. Dozens of families and law enforcement officials filled the rotunda during the ceremony.
Story continues below
“They [the four Iowans being honored] will tell you they just did what anyone else would have done. But we know not everyone runs toward danger. Not everyone steps into harm’s way. And not everyone puts their own life on the line for a stranger, a neighbor, or even a loved one. But they did,” said Reynolds.
Meagan Murray of New Hampton received the Lifesaving award, which is granted to individuals who have attempted to save another person.
Murray saved an 85-year-old woman from a house fire in September 2024 by forcing open a door to help the woman escape the flames.
“On that day, an elderly mom was in need of a guardian angel, and Megan fit the bill for her brave and selfless efforts,” said DPS Commissioner Stephan Bayens.
Michael Edwards of Clinton was awarded a Lifesaving with Valor award, which is granted to individuals who attempt to save someone’s life while putting their own life at risk.
Edwards saved a lifelong friend in February 2025 after his friend slid shin-deep into 20 feet of ice water while the pair went ice fishing.
“Absent a friendship that spanned decades, the outcome would have undoubtedly been different,” said Bayens.
Kyle Peterson of Spirit Lake was also granted a Lifesaving with Valor Award. While on a date with his wife in January 2025, Peterson witnessed an ATV crash through the ice. Without hesitation, he ran to the ice and rescued the couple inside the frigid water.
Peterson was noticeably overwhelmed with emotion during the ceremony, while the crowd was overwhelmed by his actions.
“We have a little bit of a running joke at the Department of Public Safety as when you turn 50 as a man, you suddenly, your ability to get teary grows exponentially. And I thought I could keep it together, but then I saw Kyle and I lost it,” said Bayens.
The final award recipient was John Wonio of Des Moines, who also received a Lifesaving with Valor award.
In December 2024, Wonio ran into a burning home to save his neighbors. The couple inside the home have since recovered and were discharged in time for Christmas.
“John gave his neighbors a Christmas gift they will never forget, the gift of life, for his quick and heroic actions in the face of extreme danger,” said Bayens.
